title: Composition reaches everywhere at odd index except at digons and the honeycomb's pinned ring
claim: On tori of every shape of the square, triangular and honeycomb lattices of rule-60 rings with equally spaced contacts: (1) a torus has a digon face exactly when its lattice holds (1,1) or (1,-1) (square) or a unit (honeycomb), never on the triangular lattice; on it a one-step factor of the walk polynomial vanishes in GF(2)[G], walks of two (square) or three (honeycomb) or more arcs cancel, and every contact needs at most 6 or 14 rings (at most 4 and 6 in every case read), so composition does not reach everywhere; (2) on a square torus of odd index without digons, L^(2^r - 1) is 1 exactly off (A symmetric-difference B) and the origin, A and B the images of the two diagonals. Computed, not proved: at odd index 3 to 151 a square torus composes everywhere exactly when it has no digon, every triangular torus does, and a honeycomb torus does exactly when it has no digon and is not n x n with 3 not dividing n, except one torus up to rotation of index 63; at even index (to 48) 89%, 84% and 68% of the tori without digons compose everywhere, with no rule by the lattice mod 16, the 2-part of the group or the mirror symmetries.
failure_conditions: A digon torus whose contacts need rings beyond the bound.
An odd-index torus with no digon, other than the honeycomb n x n with 3 not dividing n, on which some contact never needs some ring.
foundation_claim_scope: Tori of every shape of the square, triangular and honeycomb lattices of rule-60 rings with equally spaced law-(12,12) contacts; two-time knots only (A30); no distance.
